name: Betty McCollum

data_centers.summary: McCollum has signed on to two bills that make data center builders show their effect on local power, water and electric bills, and voted against the House budget bill that carried the state AI law freeze. She has not made her own public statements about data centers as of Sept 2026.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 7858 Data Center Community Impact Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs requiring data center builders to disclose how projects affect nearby towns' power, water and bills (joined April 15, 2026, confirmed on GovTrack).

evidence.title: Original cosponsor: H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She was an original cosponsor of a Democratic bill aimed at keeping data center energy costs off household electric bills (confirmed on GovTrack).

evidence.title: Vote: Nay on House passage of H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), the version containing the 10-year state AI law moratorium
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted against the House bill that included the AI moratorium and energy provisions, though the bill covered far more than AI so this is a weak signal.

ai_risk.summary: McCollum supports specific AI guardrails through cosponsorships: banning AI-driven price and wage discrimination and banning AI deepfakes that deceive voters. No speeches or statements of her own on AI risk were found.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 4640 Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs a ban on companies using AI and personal data to charge people different prices or pay workers different wages.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): H.R. 8858 Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She supported banning AI-made fake images, audio or video meant to trick voters in federal elections.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): H.R. 5077 CREATE AI Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: She also backs public AI research infrastructure, showing she is not anti-AI, only for targeted rules.

tech_regulation.summary: McCollum has backed targeted tech rules: protecting reproductive health data from apps and voting for the 2024 law forcing TikTok's Chinese owner to sell or face a ban. She has no record of pushing break-ups or Section 230 repeal.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): H.R. 3420 My Body, My Data Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: She supported limits on apps and companies collecting or sharing reproductive health data.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 7521 Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (TikTok divest-or-ban), March 13, 2024
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted for a targeted rule forcing TikTok's Chinese parent to sell the app or see it banned in the United States.

preemption.summary: McCollum clearly wants states to keep the power to regulate AI. She is an original cosponsor of the GUARDRAILS Act and signed both House Democratic letters opposing a state AI law moratorium and the preemption executive order.

evidence.title: Original cosponsor: H.R. 8031 GUARDRAILS Act
evidence.what_it_shows: The bill blocks the federal government from wiping out state AI laws; she joined on the day it was introduced (confirmed on GovTrack).

evidence.title: Letter: Matsui-led letter from 81 House Democrats opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and the planned preemption executive order (McCollum is a signer)
evidence.quote: our strong opposition to any effort in the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) that would reintroduce a sweeping moratorium on the ability of states and local governments to enforce their own artificial intelligence (AI) laws
evidence.what_it_shows: Her name appears in the signer list of the letter telling congressional leaders not to revive the state AI law freeze or preempt states by executive order.

evidence.title: Letter: Clarke-led letter from 44 House Democrats urging no AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA (McCollum is a signer)
evidence.quote: a moratorium would be wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation
evidence.what_it_shows: She is listed among the 44 signers asking defense bill negotiators to keep any state AI law preemption out of the NDAA.

evidence.title: Vote: Nay on House passage of H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), which contained the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted against the House bill carrying the moratorium, consistent with her letters, though the vote covered the whole budget package.

china_chips.summary: No public position found. Searches for McCollum with export controls, Nvidia, semiconductors and AI chips to China turned up nothing, and she has not cosponsored chip export bills.

signature: Quiet cosponsor: backs states' right to regulate AI (GUARDRAILS Act, two anti-moratorium letters) and data center ratepayer bills, but rarely speaks about AI herself.
groups: Ranking Member, House Appropriations Subcommittee on Defense (119th Congress)
search_notes: About 12 searches plus a site listing of mccollum.house.gov. Her own site shows no AI, data center or Big Tech press releases; Google News results about her AI or data centers were all about other people. Verified on GovTrack: original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 and H.R. 8031, cosponsor of H.R. 7858 (Apr 15, 2026); Nay on H.R. 1 House passage May 22, 2025; Yea on the 2024 TikTok bill. Verified her name in the Matsui letter PDF (extracted text) and the Clarke letter signer list. Could not verify the Markey/McClellan EPA data center air permit letter lead: markey.senate.gov returned 403 with no archive copy, so it is left out. No own statements on AI found as of Sept 12, 2026.

name: Ilhan Omar

data_centers.summary: Omar says data centers strain the grid, raise electric bills and hurt the environment, and wants transparency, community benefit agreements and a real say for residents. She cosponsors two bills on data center costs but has not joined the AI data center moratorium bill.

evidence.title: Hearing remarks: Omar opening statement at Workforce Protections hearing on AI and workplace safety
evidence.quote: The data centers that power AI and other technologies consume enormous amounts of energy, which can strain aging infrastructure, drive up electricity bills, and have adverse effects on the environment.
evidence.what_it_shows: In her own words she frames data centers as a cost to communities and calls for transparency, accountability and community benefit agreements.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 7858 Data Center Community Impact Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs making data center builders show how projects affect local power, water and bills (confirmed on GovTrack).

evidence.title: Original cosponsor: H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She was an original cosponsor of a bill to keep data center energy costs off household bills (confirmed on GovTrack); she is not a cosponsor of H.R. 9442, the AI data center moratorium bill.

ai_risk.summary: Omar wants binding guardrails on how AI is used on workers: limits on surveillance and speed quotas, bias testing, transparency in gig-work algorithms, and human control of AI weapons. She rejects the argument that government must keep its hands off AI, but her focus is specific harms rather than existential risk.

evidence.title: Hearing remarks: Omar opening statement at hearing on AI's role in workplace safety
evidence.quote: But we do need government to act. From invasive surveillance systems to dangerous work speed quotas, the workplace risks posed by these automated technologies are real and immediate.
evidence.what_it_shows: She explicitly rejects the hands-off view and calls for government rules on workplace AI.

evidence.title: Hearing remarks: Omar opening statement at the 7th Education and Workforce hearing on AI's impact on workers
evidence.quote: a bold pro-worker AI agenda must help more workers join unions, place appropriate limits on AI, safeguard worker privacy, and enforce worker protections.
evidence.what_it_shows: She lays out a guardrails agenda and faults Republicans for holding seven AI hearings without producing any bill to protect workers.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 5511 Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports requiring companies to test automated decision systems for bias and harm and report results to the FTC.

evidence.title: Press release: Omar submits nine NDAA amendments, including two on human control of AI-enabled weapons
evidence.quote: Clarifies that the Department of Defense's policy requiring human oversight of AI-enabled weapons applies to determining, tracking, engaging, and targeting decisions.
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants stronger congressional oversight of Pentagon AI and meaningful human command over autonomous weapons.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): H.R. 2894 Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: She backed a law saying a human, not an AI, must always decide to launch a nuclear weapon.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 3562 DEFIANCE Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports letting victims sue over AI-made sexual deepfakes.

evidence.title: Statement to HuffPost after an AI deepfake attack ad depicted her with Rep. Massie
evidence.quote: Campaign attack ads are generally misleading, but AI-generated ads like this cross a line and should never have been allowed in the first place
evidence.what_it_shows: She called for an AI-generated political deepfake to be taken down, consistent with her deepfake bills.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 4640 Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs banning AI-driven personalized pricing and wage setting.

tech_regulation.summary: Omar wants broad rules for all platforms on data harvesting and privacy, calls out Big Tech's access to Americans' data, and sponsors a bill putting guardrails on gig-work algorithms. She opposed the TikTok divest-or-ban law as singling out one platform, so her record is strong on regulation but mixed on bans.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Omar statement on proposals to ban TikTok
evidence.quote: We should create actual standards and regulations around data harvesting and privacy violations across social media companies
evidence.what_it_shows: She favors comprehensive privacy and data rules for every platform rather than banning one app.

evidence.title: Vote: Nay on H.R. 7521 TikTok divest-or-ban bill, March 13, 2024
evidence.what_it_shows: She was one of 65 House members to vote against forcing TikTok's Chinese owner to sell, a contrary data point on targeted tech bans.

evidence.title: MinnPost: Minnesota lawmakers disagree on TikTok (Omar's explanation of her vote)
evidence.quote: raises concerns about the First Amendment
evidence.what_it_shows: She said the bill raised free speech concerns and that Congress should set a standard for all social media platforms, not just TikTok.

evidence.title: Hearing remarks: Omar on Big Tech access to Americans' data (AI and workplace safety hearing)
evidence.quote: under the Trump Administration, we have seen an eagerness to grant Big Tech corporations unprecedented access to Americans’ data while rolling back guidance intended to protect workers and promote workplace safety.
evidence.what_it_shows: She criticizes Big Tech's data access and describes AI hype as a story told by a small number of powerful companies.

evidence.title: Press release: Omar, Jayapal, Norcross introduce the Empowering App-Based Workers Act
evidence.quote: App-based corporations have hidden behind AI algorithms and predatory take rates while drivers’ pay shrinks and executive profits soar
evidence.what_it_shows: She co-leads a bill putting transparency and anti-discrimination guardrails on the algorithms of Uber, Lyft, DoorDash and Amazon.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): H.R. 8622 Preventing the Algorithmic Facilitation of Rental Housing Cartels Act of 2024
evidence.what_it_shows: She backed outlawing landlords' use of shared pricing software to push up rents.

preemption.summary: Omar praises states that passed their own AI guardrails and criticizes the Trump administration for undermining state AI laws and seeking to preempt regulation. She did not sign the Matsui or Clarke letters and has not cosponsored the GUARDRAILS Act, so the evidence is her own hearing remarks.

evidence.title: Hearing remarks: Omar opening statement at the 7th hearing on AI's impact on workers
evidence.quote: the Trump Administration is actively undermining these states’ AI laws and looking to pass legislation to preempt any regulation.
evidence.what_it_shows: She sides with states that passed AI worker protections and objects to federal preemption.

evidence.title: Vote: Nay on House passage of H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), which contained the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted against the House bill carrying the moratorium, though the vote covered the entire budget package.

china_chips.summary: No public position found on AI chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China as of Sept 2026. Her only China-tech statements concern TikTok, where she opposed a ban of a single platform.

signature: Ranking Democrat on the House Workforce Protections subcommittee; uses its AI hearings to push worker guardrails, data center accountability and against preempting state AI laws.

notable_quote.text: Because when we unleash technology without guardrails, workers will always pay the price.

groups: Ranking Member, House Education and Workforce Subcommittee on Workforce Protections (119th Congress)
search_notes: About 12 searches plus site listings and curl of omar.house.gov press release pages. Read in full: Feb 11 and Apr 17, 2026 hearing remarks, June 30, 2026 NDAA amendments release, Dec 2025 app-based workers release, 2023 TikTok statement, Sept 2, 2026 deregulation remarks (no AI content). Verified on GovTrack: original cosponsor H.R. 7977, cosponsor H.R. 7858 (Mar 26, 2026), NOT a cosponsor of H.R. 9442 moratorium bill; Nay on H.R. 1 (May 2025) and on the 2024 TikTok bill. Not found in the Matsui letter PDF text or the Clarke letter list. The Defending Our Values PAC lead in the state file concerned AL-2, not Omar, so it was dropped. HR Executive article on the April hearing could not be opened; no chips or export control statements found.

name: Tom Emmer

data_centers.summary: Emmer is Minnesota's strongest voice for building data centers fast. He endorsed Trump's claim that communities rejecting data centers will end up 'backwards and poor,' says slowing them helps China, and told Fox Business that Congress getting in the way slows and eventually stops innovation. A proposed data center in Monticello sits in his district.

evidence.title: X post by Emmer (@GOPMajorityWhip) endorsing Trump's data center message, as quoted by MinnPost
evidence.quote: President Trump is absolutely spot on. Communist China and our adversaries would love it if the United States was asleep at the wheel and stopped innovating and developing AI and emerging tech.
evidence.what_it_shows: He immediately embraced Trump's post that towns opposing data centers will be backwards and poor, framing data centers as a China race, while other Minnesota Republicans stressed local control.

evidence.title: Fox Business interview (headline only): Rep Tom Emmer: Congress getting in the way of data centers slows and eventually stops innovation
evidence.what_it_shows: The Fox Business headline records him arguing against congressional limits on data centers; the video page itself could not be opened, so only the headline is used.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on House passage of H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), the budget bill with energy provisions and the state AI law moratorium
evidence.what_it_shows: As Majority Whip he whipped and voted for the Republican budget bill; the state context file also lists him as Yea on the GRID Power Act and Reliable Power Act.

ai_risk.summary: Emmer treats AI as a race with China where the danger is falling behind, not the technology itself, and he is backed by the pro-industry Leading the Future super PAC. He has not called for binding AI safety rules, but he also has not spoken against all regulation.

evidence.title: X post by Emmer on AI and China, as quoted by MinnPost
evidence.quote: Communist China and our adversaries would love it if the United States was asleep at the wheel and stopped innovating and developing AI and emerging tech. Thanks to President Trump’s work, the USA will be a digital LEADER!
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI policy as beating China through innovation, the classic light-touch argument.

evidence.title: PAC: Leading the Future names Emmer on its first list of 'House GOP Champions'
evidence.quote: proud to support these conservative leaders who understand the importance of keeping the United States the global leader in AI innovation
evidence.what_it_shows: The AI industry super PAC endorsed him as a pro-innovation ally, a signal of where he sits on AI rules.

evidence.title: Fox Business interview (headline only): Congress getting in the way of data centers slows and eventually stops innovation
evidence.what_it_shows: He argues congressional intervention in AI infrastructure slows innovation; headline only, the video page could not be opened.

evidence.title: Committee role: Vice Chairman, House Financial Services Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology, and Artificial Intelligence
evidence.what_it_shows: He holds a leadership seat on the subcommittee overseeing AI in finance, where his record is focused on crypto and fintech innovation.

tech_regulation.summary: Emmer's tech record is mixed. He voted for the 2024 law forcing TikTok's Chinese owner to sell, calling the app a Chinese spy app, and he pushes financial privacy bills against government surveillance. He has no record of backing broad Big Tech regulation such as kids' online safety or Section 230 changes.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 7521 TikTok divest-or-ban bill, March 13, 2024
evidence.what_it_shows: He supported a targeted rule forcing TikTok's Chinese parent to sell or face a U.S. ban.

evidence.title: X post by Emmer on the TikTok vote, as quoted by MinnPost
evidence.quote: TikTok is a (Chinese Communist Party) spy app. Plain and simple
evidence.what_it_shows: He framed the TikTok law as protecting Americans' data from China, not as general tech regulation.

preemption.summary: Emmer has not spoken directly about preempting state AI laws. As Majority Whip he voted for the House budget bill that carried the 10-year state AI law moratorium, and the Leading the Future super PAC that endorsed him says its champions will advance a national AI framework in Congress.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on House passage of H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), which contained the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted for, and as Whip helped pass, the House version containing the moratorium; the vote covered the whole budget package so it is a weak signal on its own.

evidence.title: PAC: Leading the Future endorsement statement on a national AI framework
evidence.quote: these House members will be critical to advancing a national framework in Congress that sets basic safety standards, protects children and families, and ensures America leads with confidence.
evidence.what_it_shows: The PAC backing him expects its champions to push one national AI standard, the industry's preferred alternative to state laws.

china_chips.summary: No public position found on AI chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China as of Sept 2026. He talks about beating Communist China on AI but has not addressed chip sales or the Chip Security Act.

signature: House Majority Whip and Leading the Future 'champion'; the loudest Minnesota voice for building data centers fast to beat China.

notable_quote.text: President Trump is absolutely spot on. Communist China and our adversaries would love it if the United States was asleep at the wheel and stopped innovating and developing AI and emerging tech.

groups: Vice Chairman, House Financial Services Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology, and Artificial Intelligence (119th Congress)
search_notes: About 14 searches plus a site listing and WebFetch of emmer.house.gov press releases (no AI, data center or China chip releases; older items are on crypto, fintech and financial privacy). Verified the X post quote and the Monticello district link in the MinnPost Sept 3, 2026 article; the Fox Business Aug 28, 2026 video URL could not be decoded from Google News, so it is cited by headline only. Verified Leading the Future endorsement in Breitbart, vice chairman role on the Financial Services committee site, Yea on H.R. 1 (May 2025) and on the 2024 TikTok bill on GovTrack. Not found: any statement on the Dec 2025 preemption executive order, the March 2026 White House framework, or chip export controls; the KARE11 Dec 2025 preemption article and The Block 2024 crypto-AI interview could not be opened. The Congressional Crypto Caucus co-chair lead was not verified and is not AI-related, so it is omitted from groups.
